title: docs(architecture): add workspace layout and module dependency map
problem: There is no single document describing the workspace layout and which modules may depend on which, so architectural intent is implicit in imports.
why: New contributors and reviewers need a map to place code correctly and avoid layering violations.
scope: Document the two crates, every core module, and their intended dependency directions.
Include a short diagram and a note on which modules are public API.
guidance: Generate the module list from the actual tree so it cannot drift silently.

title: docs(adr): add ADR-0003 determinism contract
problem: Determinism is a core promise but is only stated in code comments, not recorded as a decision.
why: A written contract prevents future contributors from introducing ordering, time, or randomness dependence.
scope: Record sorting rules, fingerprint stability, and forbidden inputs (wall clock, RNG, filesystem order).
guidance: Reference the deterministic-outcome tests as enforcement.

title: docs(adr): add ADR-0004 error-handling strategy
problem: The split between `ScanError` (library) and `CliError` (CLI) and the no-panic policy is undocumented.
why: Consistent error handling keeps the scanner safe on untrusted input and preserves exit-code semantics.
scope: Document when to use `ScanError`, when diagnostics are preferred over errors, and the no-panic rule.
guidance: Reference how parser failures become diagnostics.

title: docs(adr): add ADR-0005 dependency justification policy
problem: There is no written rule for when a new dependency may be added.
why: The scanner's trustworthiness depends on a small, auditable dependency surface.
scope: State the criteria, the review requirement, and the `cargo-deny` gate.

title: test(arch): enforce crate and module dependency boundaries
problem: Nothing prevents `soroban-scan-core` from gaining a dependency on the CLI or from creating module cycles.
why: Layering violations erode the reusable library API and complicate testing.
scope: Add a test asserting the core crate does not depend on the CLI crate.
Add a check that `report` depends on engine but not vice versa, and similar documented directions.
guidance: Parse `Cargo.toml` files and scan `use` statements for cross-module edges.
acceptance: Boundary test fails when a violation is introduced
tests: A deliberately failing example in a comment

title: feat(tooling): add a task runner for common workflows
problem: Contributors must remember several commands for format, clippy, tests, docs, and benchmarks.
why: A single entry point reduces mistakes and speeds onboarding.
guidance: Document in the setup guide; keep recipes thin wrappers over cargo.
tests: CI invokes one recipe to prove it works

title: feat(tooling): add an xtask crate for repository automation
problem: Repository automation is spread across Python scripts with no shared, typed entry point.
why: A single Rust `xtask` is portable, testable, and consistent with the toolchain already required.
scope: Add a workspace `xtask` binary with subcommands for fixture scaffolding, docs link checking, and backlog generation.
guidance: Keep the existing Python tools working until xtask reaches parity.
acceptance: At least one existing script reimplemented
security: Automation must stay offline and non-destructive.

title: chore(repo): add CODEOWNERS
problem: Review routing is manual; there are no default reviewers for security-sensitive paths.
why: Code ownership improves review latency and ensures sensitive paths get adequate review.
scope: Add `.github/CODEOWNERS` assigning the security-sensitive paths (rules, engine, security docs).
guidance: Keep ownership broad enough to avoid blocking contributions.

title: docs(governance): add GOVERNANCE.md
problem: Decision-making, maintainer roles, and how proposals are accepted are undefined.
why: Clear governance helps contributors know how to propose and land changes.
scope: Describe roles, the ADR process, and how contentious changes are decided.
guidance: Keep it lightweight and consistent with the contributor roadmap.
acceptance: GOVERNANCE.md merged and linked from README/CONTRIBUTING

title: docs(api): define a public API stability policy for the core crate
problem: It is unclear which parts of `soroban-scan-core` are stable public API and which are internal.
why: Consumers embedding the scanner need a stability guarantee; contributors need freedom to refactor internals.
scope: Classify modules as stable or unstable and document the semver implications.
guidance: Consider `#[doc(hidden)]` or a documented `internal` module boundary.
acceptance: At least one enforcement (lint or doc attribute)

title: ci(api): add cargo-semver-checks to CI
problem: Breaking changes to the public API can land unnoticed.
why: Automated semver checks prevent accidental breakage for library consumers.
scope: Add a `cargo-semver-checks` job comparing against the latest tag once one exists.
guidance: Scope the check to the core crate; tolerate pre-1.0 minor bumps explicitly.
deps: Public API stability policy; first release tag exists.
